hypothesis: Non-symplectic integrators drift in the first integrals of the geodesic flow (speed, Clairaut constant, angular momentum); adaptive local-error control accumulates a linear secular drift, while a fixed step on these closed or quasi-periodic orbits can keep the drift bounded over long stretches; bounded speed error does not guarantee the right orbit.
input_data: Torus(2, 1) start (0, 0.5) heading 0.7 (bounded oscillation about the outer equator)
Fixed step h = 0.125 for Euler, midpoint, RK4; DP45 rtol 1e-06, atol 1e-09; checkpoints L = 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320
mathematical_model: Energy g(v, v) = 1, torus Clairaut rho^2 phi' and sphere angular momentum X x X' are exact first integrals. A constant speed error gives a constant frequency error on the sphere, hence position error ~ L; a speed error growing ~ L gives position error ~ L^2. On Torus(2, 1) the orbit oscillates between |theta| <= arccos((c - R)/r); a Clairaut drift across the separatrix changes it into an orbit winding around the tube.
numerical_result: Energy exponents: adaptive torus 0.934, sphere 0.998; RK4 envelope exponent 0.0275 (torus, L = 10-160) and 0.00661 (sphere, L = 10-320), torus RK4 local slope 0.861 from L = 160 to 320; sphere position exponent RK4 1.02, adaptive 2.05; torus adaptive Clairaut exponent 1.08; fixed-step Clairaut envelopes are not described by one exponent (local slopes: Euler 1.3, 0.82, 0.5, 0.11, 0.0047, RK4 0.18, 0.23, 0.43, 0.57, 0.74); torus Euler max energy error 0.035 but max |theta| 285 versus turning latitude 1.369; sphere Euler stopped at s = 14.
observation_model: Running maxima (envelopes) of |I(s) - I(0)| at checkpoints; exponents are log-log slopes over the reached checkpoints; no renormalization at any step.
